soundcheck.heard: A Kodiak woman asked Google when Snipe Season opens. She told Troopers its AI answer said September 1st. So on September 5th, she shot three Snipe. At home, she opened the state regulations and saw her mistake. She called Troopers and turned herself in. The Troopers report says the general season opened October 8th. So the answer and the report disagreed. That Trooper ran her exact search. He got the same wrong answer. So which page can a hunter trust? She pleaded no contest and paid $150. She told the Alaska beacon, I feel terrible. State spokesman Austin McDaniel says he thinks it's the first time AI has been cited. He expects more. Weren't there warnings? There were. Google's help page says AI answers may include mistakes and to check more than one place. Google didn't respond to the beacon's request for comment on the wrong answer. McDaniel says the one source of truth is fishing games regulations and emergency orders. But that source has a catch. Fishing games own page says its online regulations are simplified and emergency orders can override them. So even the official page is a simplified summary of state law. The answer was on top. What counts sits underneath the regulations and any emergency order. Check them first. Fishing game will mail you the regulations or you can call the office. Before you hunt, what do you check?
